observations: docs/ORDERING.md line 1 is still titled 'Ordering M3-ASSY-R9 prototypes'; section 8 explicitly says it is the current R10 worksheet and sections 1-7 are R9, so no procedure is wrong (wording only).

The JLC BOM marks the eight DB125 lines 'THT (JLC THT assembly)' while ORDERING 8.2 requires hand soldering (no selective or wave); JLC's THT service includes manual soldering, so the two agree once the order remark states it (8.2 already says to).

Several 8.2 copper gaps are quoted to 0.001 mm (R102 1.997, C431 2.050, C410/C420 2.003, J3 slots 1.952/2.010/2.145 mm); this lens's polygon measurement (ERROR_INSIDE, max_error 0.005 mm) gives 2.001 / 2.055 / 2.011 and 1.958 / 2.011 / 2.150 mm, i.e. within the approximation error; not a wrong figure.

ORDERING 8.3 gives U4's 'bottom outline' as x15.1-19.1, y44.3-47.5; the courtyard is x15.125-18.875, y44.275-47.525 and the B.SilkS pin-1 mark reaches x19.065, so the stated box is the courtyard plus silk union (conservative for the 3 mm coating keep-out), not a false figure.

Global solder-mask expansion and minimum web are 0; U4's 0.150 mm webs exceed JLC's 0.10 mm green-mask pad-spacing figure; no pad pair on the board needs a dam JLC cannot hold that the records claim it will (JLC merges openings below its limit; not a stated rule violation).
Inner-layer copper in the Gerber job file stackup reads 0.030 mm (KiCad stackup default), not a fabrication instruction; the order form fixes 1 oz inner copper and the JLC041611-7628 stackup.
